y1: John the Baptist was put in prison by King Herod. John sent his disciples to ask: “Are You the one who is to come?”
y2: Jesus answered: “Go and tell what you hear and see: the blind see, the lame walk, and the Gospel is preached to the poor.” Jesus is the one who was to come.
y4: Jesus talked about children in the market: “We played the flute for you, and you didn't dance. We sang a sad song, and you didn't cry.”
y5: The people didn't like John, and they didn't like Jesus either. No matter what happened, they didn't open their hearts.
y7: Jesus prayed: “Father, I thank You that You have hidden these things from the wise and smart, and revealed them to little children.”
y8: God's Kingdom is understood not by smart people, but by those who open their hearts like a child. This is greater than wisdom.
y10: Jesus said: “Come to Me, all you who are tired and carry heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.”
y11: “I am gentle and humble in heart. My yoke is easy, and my burden is light.” When we are tired, we find peace by going to Jesus.
verse: “Come to Me, all you who are tired and carry heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.”
prayer: Jesus, thank You for calling me to 'come to Me' when I carry a heavy burden. When I am tired and in trouble, let me come to You and rest. Help me to open my heart like a child and learn from You. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: prison. A place where people who are considered guilty are kept. John the Baptist was put in prison.
d1: Gospel. The joyful news that Jesus came to save us. The Gospel is preached to the poor.
d2: flute. A musical instrument played by blowing air into it. We played the flute, and you didn't dance.
d3: wisdom. The ability to know what is right and make good choices. God's Kingdom is revealed to little children, not by human wisdom.
d4: burden. A heavy thing carried on the back. Worries and sadness in the heart are also a burden. We bring our heavy burden to Jesus.
d5: gentle. A soft and kind heart. Jesus has a gentle heart.
d6: yoke. A wooden frame put on the necks of two oxen so they can work together. Jesus' yoke is easy.
